clue.text: Among couples Frenchman gets by

indicators.note: the word Among says the Frenchman's letter sits amid the letters for couples

parts.note: couples are pairs, ties linking two things
M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman scrapes a living in the company of married couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is only a link; the definition is the single word 'by', as in six by four.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic 'by' expresses multiplication, as in three by four, the same sense as the word for multiplied.

clue.text: Warning to cancel Romeo in connection with playhouse

indicators.note: to cancel says the letter for Romeo is struck out of the warning

parts.note: a threat is a warning
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
re means concerning or in connection with

explanation.surface: A warning to cancel Romeo and Juliet is issued at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cancel' takes R out of THREAT, leaving THEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building where plays are staged.

clue.text: Schoolteacher expelling son with mother

indicators.note: expelling says the letter for son is thrown out of the teacher's word

parts.note: a master is a male schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A teacher expels a pupil whose mother is with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is the Latin for mother, old public-school slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Former Yugoslavian bins are for recycling

indicators.note: for recycling says the letters are reprocessed into a new order

explanation.surface: Bins in Belgrade are put out for the recycling collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia was a republic of the former Yugoslavia, so a Serb is one of its people.

clue.text: Old puffer in shopping centre by a road

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: An old smoker is found in a shopping mall near a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A puffer is a steam train; the Mallard is the famous British locomotive that set the steam speed record in 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mallard is a celebrated steam locomotive, and puffer is a childish name for a steam engine.

clue.text: Typical person of no fixed abode?

definitions.text: Typical person of no fixed abode?

parts.words: Typical person of no fixed abode?
parts.note: the phrase for an ordinary citizen is read literally as a homeless fellow living out on the road

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an ordinary member of the public, taken literally as a homeless man sleeping rough.

clue.text: Having large one Fawkes shortly becomes sluggish

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: shortly says the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Guy Fawkes also went by the name Guido

explanation.surface: Guy Fawkes, a big chap, becomes slow and lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes, of the 1605 Gunpowder Plot, used the name Guido; 'shortly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid describes someone slow-moving and lacking energy.

clue.text: Soaking for sailor, extremely dishonest, accepting rupees

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: accepting says the letter for rupees is taken inside

parts.note: so means extremely, as in so tired
bent is slang for dishonest or corrupt
R is the abbreviation for rupees, Indian currency

explanation.surface: A very crooked sailor takes rupees in bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts R inside SOBENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent material soaks up liquid, so it is soaking in that active sense.

clue.text: Thomas and Lynda going out

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters change and rearrange as though off on a date

explanation.surface: Thomas and Lynda are dating.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas was the Welsh poet; 'Thomas' is the surname for the first name sought.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Dylan Thomas carried this first name.

clue.text: These characters with LONDON LANDLORDS?

parts.note: the words London landlords are printed in big upper-case type, and London landlords lease property in the nation's main city

explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case type shows the words, and people who let out rooms in the main city are its other sense.

clue.text: Use 4A — run away with nurse

parts.note: to enter data or a building is to make use of it

indicators.note: run is R in cricket scoring, and away says that letter leaves the word for the locomotive

parts.note: the answer at 4 across names a famous steam locomotive, so the cross-reference stands for a train

explanation.surface: Someone told to use a duck flees with a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at MALLARD, but what it supplies is the kind of thing a Mallard is, a TRAIN; 'run away' removes R (run, in cricket) to leave TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or grudge is to entertain it, holding it in the mind.

clue.text: Aslan with fractures in the nose

indicators.note: something with fractures is broken, so the lion's name is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Narnia's lion suffers a broken nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Aslan is the lion of C. S. Lewis's Narnia books.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal describes what relates to or occurs in the nose, such as a passage or a voice.

clue.text: Ends session in Italy

parts.note: a term is a session of a school or court
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A school session finishes in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini is the plural of terminus, the end of a line or route.

clue.text: No charged element for silly rent on housing unionist

indicators.note: housing says the scrambled letters enclose the unionist's letter like a house around it
silly signals that the words rent and on are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics

explanation.surface: A tenant pays a silly rent for housing a union man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns RENT ON into NETRON, and 'housing' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle carries no electric charge, unlike its partner the proton.

clue.text: Add small measure of spirits

definitions.meaning: a small dram of whisky or rum

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both totting up a column of figures and a little nip of liquor.

clue.text: Towards North Island's stormily sea-girt country

indicators.note: girt means encircled, so the rearranged sea letters wrap around the rest
stormily says the sea is tossed about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to means towards
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A small Baltic nation is ringed by stormy waters to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-girt country' looks like a single definition, but the sea is the anagram fodder that 'stormily' scrambles and 'girt' wraps around TONI; only 'country' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, a nation bordering the Gulf of Finland.

clue.text: Particularly inferior red wine consumed after time

indicators.note: after says the word for consumed follows the time abbreviation

parts.note: tent is a dark red Spanish wine
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a measure of time
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Red wine downed after hours is of very poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT, a sweet red wine from Spain, is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenth-rate means of extremely poor quality, far down the scale.

clue.text: Single theologian in feathery layer not seen

indicators.note: in says the single and theologian letters go inside the feathery layer

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs, so a feathered layer
I is the Roman numeral one
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A lone divine buried in a bed of feathers is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feathery layer' looks like down or plumage, but it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unseen is concealed or out of view.

clue.text: Nail polish for sweetheart, old sweetheart in retirement

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the old word for a lover is read backwards

parts.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A woman's nail varnish is a keepsake from an old flame now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read literally as the heart of 'sweet', E; 'in retirement' turns LEMAN into NAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail varnish is commonly called nail enamel, a glossy hard coating.

clue.text: Important fellow at the Admiralty?

parts.note: the slang for a key person is read as a sailor on the main, the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: The slang for a chief figure is read as a seaman of the main, the high seas, fit for the navy.

clue.text: Principal replaced perhaps in recent business launch

parts.note: the star is the principal performer in a show
replaced read as put back gives the letters of put written backwards

explanation.surface: A head teacher has been replaced at a newly opened company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' is read cryptically as 'put back', giving PUT written backwards; 'perhaps' flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly founded company, a venture just getting going.

clue.text: Chief route to London tube station

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
a way is a route

explanation.surface: The main road leads to a London Underground stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Archway is a station on the Northern line of the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Archway is a stop on the London Underground in the north of the city.

clue.text: Delighted where piano hired out

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
leased means hired out

explanation.surface: A happy owner rents out the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased means glad or happy.

clue.text: Take food from 1D

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the middle of the answer at 1 down

parts.note: the answer at 1 down is the word for a playhouse

explanation.surface: Someone takes their food from a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside the answer to 1 down, the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume a meal, taking in nourishment.

clue.text: No believer in robbery

parts.note: at means in, as at home means in the house
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A person without faith is caught up in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but supplies AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects belief in any god.

clue.text: Amid dry group unopened wine seen with vessel for claret

indicators.note: amid says the trimmed wine sits between the letters of the dry group

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group whose members stay dry

indicators.note: unopened says the wine loses its first letter

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Among teetotallers, a closed bottle of wine is seen beside a claret jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is slang for blood, so its vessel is the main artery.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, the body's chief blood channel.

clue.text: Find new use for old thing on bike

definitions.text: Find new use for old thing

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
a cycle is a bike

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fresh purpose for an old bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle is to process waste so it can be put to further service.

clue.text: Where miners survived something very hot or rather cold upon the tongue?

indicators.note: upon the tongue says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.words: something very hot or rather cold
parts.note: a hot pepper and the adjective for cool weather share the same spoken form

explanation.surface: A miners' rescue story turns on something spicy or chilly to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both chilli (hot pepper) and chilly (cold) sound like the country, where 33 trapped miners were rescued in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2010 thirty-three miners trapped underground at San Jose were rescued in this South American country.

clue.text: Kingdom's silver coin and money supply

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
M is the economists' symbol for money supply, as in M1 and M4

explanation.surface: A monarchy's silver coinage makes up its money supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Kingdom stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: European travelling sees wild flower as national symbol

indicators.note: travelling says the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A European tourist sees a wild bloom that stands for a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild flower' wants to be the definition, but 'wild' is part of the shuffled fodder with 'sees'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine bloom is a national emblem of Austria and Switzerland.

clue.text: Area right inside second planet's infernal regions

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right goes within the planet's name

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the Sun

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the second planet lies a hellish landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Avernus is a crater lake near Naples that the Romans held to be the entrance to the underworld, and the name came to mean the underworld itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin poetry the name stands for the underworld, the abode of the dead.

clue.text: Give in return

definitions.meaning: to give in is to surrender or concede
a return on an investment is the profit it makes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to surrender and the income an investment produces.
